mainTopic: The extra goat of יום הכפורים and the views of רב, רבי יוחנן, and רבי יהודה; the scapegoat that dies; and whether this year's offerings and שקלים can serve next year.
overview: One goat of the יום הכפורים pair died, so a new pair was brought, and now there is one goat too many. רב says the surviving goat of the first pair is offered and the extra goat of the second pair grazes. רבי יוחנן says the second pair's goat is offered and the first pair's leftover goat grazes. The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's view fits a rule everyone accepts. It then challenges רב by comparing his case to setting aside two backup חטאות, and answers that רב follows רבי יוסי. Next it tests both views against רבי יהודה's rulings in the משנה. In one version, the word 'ועוד' remains a difficulty for רבי יוחנן. The גמרא then uses a פסוק to explain why, for רבי יהודה, the scapegoat must stay alive until its partner's blood is applied. Finally, it brings a משנה about lost שקלים, where רבי יהודה lets them count for next year. רבא says the reason is that this year's offerings can be brought next year. אביי challenges this from lost יום הכפורים offerings, and רבא's reply begins on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: if atonement came through the animal that was never lost, the lost one dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states a rule that all opinions accept: if a person atoned with the animal that was never lost, the found 'lost' חטאת is put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that if a person gained atonement through the animal that was not lost, the lost animal is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a 'בשלמא' (it works well for) argument that began on the previous amud: it shows why רבי יוחנן's view works, using a rule all sides accept. If someone's חטאת got lost, he set aside a replacement, and he brought the replacement (the one that was never lost), then the original lost animal must die. The next step ('אלא לרב') turns this into a question on רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some cases of a lost חטאת are disputed. This one is not. Once the owner was atoned through the animal that never went missing, the earlier lost animal falls under the rule of חטאת שמתה and is left to die. This shared starting point becomes the measuring stick for the challenge to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
He gained atonement
The lost animal (a sin-offering that went missing)
Is left to die (it is locked away until it dies)

phrases.english: Everyone agrees
that if he gained atonement through the one that was not lost —
phrases.notes: The animal that never went missing, i.e., the replacement.

phrases.english: the lost one is left to die.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם נִתְכַּפֵּר בְּשֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲבוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא לרבי יוחנן' half of an argument begun on the previous amud. It explains why, for רבי יוחנן, an individual's leftover animal in this case would die. This sets up the 'אלא לרב' challenge in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When atonement came through the never-lost animal, the lost one is put to death, according to all opinions.

steps.title: Challenge to רב: his case looks like setting aside two sin-offerings as backup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that in רב's view the case resembles designating two חטאות for backup. According to רבי אושעיא, the extra animal there simply grazes, so no special reason should be needed for רב's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב, it is like someone who sets aside two sin-offerings as a guarantee. And רבי אושעיא said: if one set aside two sin-offerings as a guarantee, he gains atonement with one of them, and the second is left to graze.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with how רב's case is being explained. In רב's view, the first goat was never pushed aside, so the second pair's goat looks like a simple backup animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's view, the surviving goat from the first pair stays valid, so the new goat was only an extra 'just in case' animal. רבי אושעיא rules that when two animals are set aside as backup, one is offered and the other grazes (it does not die), even for an individual. So for רב, grazing should not depend on this being a communal offering: even an individual's extra animal here would graze. That contradicts the assumption that only a communal חטאת grazes, while an individual's would die.

keyTerms.meaning: But / rather (introduces a challenge)
One who sets aside (designates) an animal
As a guarantee or backup, in case one is lost
It is left to graze until it gets a blemish, then it is sold

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'grazes' (תרעה) and 'dies' (מתה). Grazing is the milder outcome: the animal is eventually redeemed. Dying means it is locked away until it dies.

phrases.english: But according to Rav,
it is like one who sets aside
two sin-offerings as a guarantee,
and Rabbi Oshaya said:
if one set aside two sin-offerings as a guarantee —
he gains atonement with one of them,
and the second is left to graze.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַב הָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּמַפְרִישׁ שְׁתֵּי חַטָּאוֹת לְאַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the laws of designated sin-offerings to question how רב's case should be classified.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that, in רב's view, the extra goat grazes only because it is a communal חטאת (an individual's would die).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רב's view the first goat is never disqualified, so the new goat is just a backup. By רבי אושעיא's rule, a backup animal grazes even for an individual. So for רב there should be no difference between communal and individual here; even an individual's extra animal would graze.

steps.title: Answer: רב follows רבי יוסי, so the second animal was designated 'to be lost' from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב follows רבי יוסי, who says the מצוה is done with the first animal. So the second animal is treated from the start as one designated to be lost, not as a true backup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבא said that רב holds like רבי יוסי, who said the מצוה is done with the first one, the second animal is considered from the beginning like one set aside to be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because רב holds like רבי יוסי, the second animal is not a real backup. It counts as an animal designated 'to be lost.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוסי, the מצוה must be done with the first animal. So when the second one was set aside, it was already destined never to be used, as if designated 'for loss.' That is different from רבי אושעיא's backup case, where either animal could be the one offered. So for an individual, such an animal would die, and רב's case is not like רבי אושעיא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
Holds in accordance with
The מצוה should be done with the first animal
From the very beginning
For loss (designated to end up unused)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the outcome for an extra animal depends on its status at the moment it was designated: a real backup grazes, while an animal designated 'to be lost' would die.

phrases.english: Since Rava said:
Rav holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei
who said the מצוה is with the first one,
from the beginning it is like one designated to be lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רָבָא רַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the case: it is not a backup designation but a designation 'for loss.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second goat is a backup like רבי אושעיא's case, so it simply grazes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because רב follows רבי יוסי, the second goat was designated 'to be lost' from the start, so רבי אושעיא's backup rule does not apply.

steps.title: Opening a challenge from רבי יהודה's ruling that the extra goat dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה, who says the extra goat dies. It shows this fits easily with רבי יוחנן, which sets up a difficulty for רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says it should die. Granted, according to רבי יוחנן, who said the second goat of the first pair grazes, when רבי יהודה says it dies, that works: atonement came through the second goat of the second pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes רבי יהודה's ruling that the leftover goat dies and first shows why that works well for רבי יוחנן. The question on רב comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the goat from the second pair is the one offered, so the leftover goat from the first pair is like a lost animal whose owner atoned with a never-lost one. By the rule in step 1, such a lost animal dies, which matches רבי יהודה. The 'בשלמא' (granted) format signals that רב's view will have trouble explaining רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Granted / it works well for (one side), setting up a difficulty for the other
A pair (of goats)
It should graze
It should die

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the first half of a בשלמא argument. Do not expect the question on רב here; it comes next.

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Yehuda says: It should die.
Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said the second goat of the first pair should graze,
according to Rabbi Yehuda, it should die —
since he gains atonement with the second goat of the second pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תָּמוּת. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the first challenge, the גמרא opens a new challenge to רב from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the goat from the first pair is the one offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's 'it dies' fits רבי יוחנן, since atonement came through the never-lost second-pair goat. The implied question is how רב, who offers the first-pair goat, can explain רבי יהודה's ruling.

steps.title: According to רב, how does רבי יהודה's view allow any atonement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב: if רבי יהודה says the second goat of the second pair dies, no goat seems to be left for the atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב, who said that the second goat of the second pair grazes (according to the חכמים), and according to רבי יהודה it is left to die: according to רבי יהודה, with which goat does he get atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רב's reading of רבי יהודה. If the extra goat of the new pair must die, which goat is left to bring the atonement?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a living animal that was once pushed away from the altar stays pushed away for good (בעלי חיים נדחין). So the leftover goat from the first pair cannot be used. If, as רב says, רבי יהודה also makes the second goat of the second pair die, then it seems no goat remains to atone with.

keyTerms.meaning: The first pair / the second pair of goats used for the lottery on יום הכפורים
It grazes until it gets a blemish, then it is sold
It is left to die
With what does he get atonement?

phrases.english: But according to Rav, who said
the second goat of the second pair should graze,
phrases.notes: This is the view of the חכמים according to רב.

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Yehuda it should die —
then according to Rabbi Yehuda, with which goat does he gain atonement?
phrases.notes: The first pair's leftover goat is permanently rejected, and this one dies. Nothing seems to be left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 4 showed that רבי יהודה fits רבי יוחנן. Now the גמרא turns to רב and asks how רבי יהודה's ruling could work in his view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that, according to רבי יהודה, the second goat of the second pair dies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה rejects the first pair's goat permanently. If the second pair's extra goat also dies, no valid goat remains to atone with.

steps.title: רבי יהודה was talking about the first pair's goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's "it dies" refers to the second goat of the first pair, not the second pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think רבי יהודה was talking about the second goat of the second pair? רבי יהודה was talking about the second goat of the first pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying we misread which goat רבי יהודה meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat that dies, according to רבי יהודה, is the leftover goat from the first pair, which he holds is permanently rejected. The second pair's goat is still available, so it is the one that brings the atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think…? (introduces a correction of a wrong assumption)
Is referring to, is standing on

steps.confusionAlert: There are four goats in play. רבי יהודה's "it dies" is about the leftover goat from the FIRST pair. The second pair is used for the service.

phrases.english: Do you think that Rabbi Yehuda
was referring to the second goat of the second pair?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן קָאֵי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda was referring to the second goat of the first pair.
phrases.notes: So the second pair's goat is offered and brings the atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג שֵׁנִי קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which case the statement refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה's "it dies" refers to the extra goat of the second pair, so nothing is left to atone with.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to the extra goat of the first pair. The second pair stays available for atonement.

steps.title: Another version of the challenge quotes רבי יהודה's 'furthermore'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a different version of the objection, starting by quoting רבי יהודה's second ruling in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some raise the objection like this: "And furthermore רבי יהודה said: if the blood spilled, the scapegoat dies. If the scapegoat died, the blood is spilled."
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא opens a second version of the challenge and first quotes the משנה it will build on. The actual point comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the earlier challenge, these people use the word "ועוד" ("and furthermore") in the משנה. That word suggests רבי יהודה is adding a new, separate point beyond his first ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And some raise the objection this way (another version)
And furthermore — signals a new, additional point
The goat sent away to עזאזל (the scapegoat)
The blood spilled before it was sprinkled

phrases.english: And there are those who raise the objection like this:
And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
If the blood spilled, the scapegoat is left to die,
if the scapegoat died, the blood should be spilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the challenge, replacing steps 4–6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position (completed in the next step).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "ועוד" means רבי יהודה's second ruling must be a new and different point.

steps.title: 'Furthermore' fits רב but not רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: For רב, the two halves of the משנה are two separate disputes, so "ועוד" makes sense. For רבי יוחנן, "ועוד" has no clear meaning. The question stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רב: the first part argues about a communal חטאת, and the last part argues about whether living animals are rejected. But according to רבי יוחנן, what is the "furthermore"? It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the word "ועוד" matches רב's view but not רבי יוחנן's. The challenge to רבי יוחנן is left unresolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's view, the first part of the משנה is a dispute about a leftover communal חטאת (graze or die). The second part is a different dispute: whether a living animal that was disqualified stays rejected (בעלי חיים נדחין). That is truly a new point, so "ועוד" fits. According to רבי יוחנן, even the חכמים agree the first pair's leftover goat is rejected, so there is no separate new dispute for "ועוד" to add.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for… (sets up a contrast with a view that does not work)
The first clause / the last clause of the משנה
A sin-offering brought for the whole community
Living animals can be permanently rejected from the altar
It is a difficulty — the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The single word "ועוד" shows that רבי יהודה is raising two separate disputes. That fits רב, and it remains an unanswered difficulty for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא can test a view using one small word in the משנה. The word "ועוד" must mean a new idea.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav,
in the first clause they disagree about a communal sin-offering
phrases.notes: Whether the leftover animal grazes or dies.

phrases.english: and in the latter clause they disagree about living animals
phrases.notes: Whether a disqualified living animal stays rejected.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, what is the meaning of "and furthermore"?
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב, רֵישָׁא פְּלִיגִי בְּחַטַּאת צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up by the quote in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's understanding of the dispute in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "ועוד" requires a second, separate dispute. Only רב's reading provides one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against רבי יוחנן from the word "ועוד" stays unanswered (קשיא).

steps.title: Why spilled blood makes the scapegoat die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's ruling and says the first half makes sense, because the blood's מצוה was not yet done. This prepares a question on the second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And furthermore רבי יהודה said: if the blood spilled, the scapegoat dies." It makes sense that if the blood spilled the scapegoat dies, because its מצוה has not been done yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new discussion of the משנה. It explains the first half of רבי יהודה's ruling, and this sets up a question on the second half ("if the scapegoat died, the blood is spilled"), which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood of the goat for ה׳ spilled before it was sprinkled, its מצוה was never finished. A new pair must be brought, and the old scapegoat is not used. The word "בשלמא" tells us the next half will be harder to explain: in that case the blood's job could still be done.

keyTerms.meaning: Because still / not yet
Its מצוה has not been done

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
If the blood spilled — the scapegoat is left to die.
Granted, if the blood spilled, the scapegoat should die —
because its מצוה has not yet been performed.
phrases.notes: The blood was never sprinkled, so the service must start again with a new pair.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם — יָמוּת הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ. בִּשְׁלָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the רב / רבי יוחנן discussion, the גמרא quotes the משנה again for a new purpose: to explain רבי יהודה's ruling itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setting up why the second half ("if the scapegoat died, the blood is spilled") is justified, since the blood could still be used.

steps.title: Why should the scapegoat's death ruin the other goat's blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second half of רבי יהודה's ruling. If the שעיר המשתלח dies, why should the blood of the שעיר לה׳ be spilled out? The משתלח's מצוה has already been done.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the sent-away goat died, why should the blood be poured out? Its מצוה has already been done!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the question it set up in Step 9. It attacks the second half of רבי יהודה's ruling: why does the scapegoat's death ruin the blood of the other goat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first half, the blood was still waiting to be used, so its loss made sense. Here the שעיר המשתלח already had its essential part done through the lottery. So why should its later death disqualify the blood of its partner, the שעיר לה׳?

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל (the scapegoat)
The blood is poured out (it becomes unusable)
Its מצוה has already been done

phrases.english: But if the sent-away goat died,
why should the blood be poured out?
phrases.notes: The blood of the שעיר לה׳ that was already slaughtered.

phrases.english: Its מצוה has already been done!
phrases.notes: The lottery, the essential part, already happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵת הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ, אַמַּאי יִשָּׁפֵךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the question that Step 9 prepared, now aimed at the second half of רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that if the שעיר המשתלח dies, the blood of the שעיר לה׳ is poured out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משתלח's essential מצוה is already done, so its death should have no effect on its partner's blood.

steps.title: The scapegoat must stay alive until its partner's blood is applied
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי bring the פסוק ״יעמד חי לפני ה׳ לכפר״. It teaches that the שעיר המשתלח must stay alive until the blood of its partner is applied. If it dies before then, the blood is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רבי ינאי said: The פסוק says, ״It shall be stood alive before ה׳ to atone.״ Until when must it stay alive? Until the time the blood of its partner is applied.
steps.whatsHappening: The students of רבי ינאי answer the question from a פסוק. The scapegoat has one more job: it must stay alive until the other goat's blood is applied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the משתלח's job was finished after the lottery. The פסוק adds a requirement: it must be 'alive' for the atonement, and that lasts until its partner's blood is applied. So if it dies first, the atonement through the blood cannot be completed, and the blood is poured out.

keyTerms.meaning: The students (house) of רבי ינאי said
The פסוק says
It shall be stood alive
The applying (sprinkling) of the blood
Its partner (here, the שעיר לה׳)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the שעיר המשתלח must stay alive until the blood of the שעיר לה׳ is applied. That is why its death before then ruins the blood.

phrases.english: The students of the house of Rabbi Yannai said:
The verse says:
"It shall be stood alive before the Lord, to atone"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:י, about the שעיר המשתלח.

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי יְהֵא זָקוּק לִהְיוֹת חַי —
phrases.english: Until when must it be alive?

phrases.aramaic: עַד שְׁעַת מַתַּן דָּמִים שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: Until the time the blood of its partner is applied.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source showing an extra requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משתלח's מצוה ended with the lottery, so its death should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק requires the משתלח to stay alive until its partner's blood is applied, so its earlier death disqualifies the blood.

steps.title: A משנה about city shekels that were stolen or lost
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת שקלים. A city sent its שקלים with messengers, and the coins were stolen or lost on the way. If the תרומת הלשכה was already taken, the messengers swear to the Temple treasurers. If not, they swear to the city's residents, and the residents must give new שקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: If a city's residents sent their שקלים and they were stolen or lost: if the withdrawal from the chamber was already made, the messengers swear to the treasurers. If not, they swear to the city's residents, and the residents give other שקלים in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from מסכת שקלים. This is setup: the גמרא is laying out this source so it can discuss it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whose loss is it depends on timing. Once the תרומת הלשכה has been taken, all שקלים already sent count as Temple property, so the Temple suffers the loss and the messengers swear to its treasurers. Before that, the coins still belong to the city, so the messengers swear to the residents, who must pay again.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Their half-shekel coins given yearly to the בית המקדש
The withdrawal of funds from the Temple chamber was made
Temple treasurers
They take an oath

steps.confusionAlert: Here תרומה does not mean the produce gift to a כהן. It means the withdrawal of coins from the Temple chamber (תרומת הלשכה) to buy the year's קרבנות.

phrases.english: We learned there:
Residents of a city who sent their shekels
and they were stolen or were lost,
if the withdrawal from the chamber had already been made —
the messengers swear to the treasurers.
phrases.notes: The coins already belong to the Temple.

phrases.english: And if not — they swear to the residents of the city,
and the residents of the city give other shekels in their place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the שעירים discussion closed in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lost שקלים are the Temple's loss if the תרומת הלשכה was already taken; otherwise they are the city's loss, and the city must pay again.

steps.title: The lost coins are found: do they count for next year?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. If the lost שקלים are found or returned, both sets are holy. The ת״ק says they do not count for next year. רבי יהודה says they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the coins were found, or the thieves gave them back, both sets (the old ones and the new ones) are holy שקלים. But they do not count toward next year. רבי יהודה says: they do count toward next year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from מסכת שקלים. It now covers the case where the lost coins show up again after the city already gave new ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The city has now given two sets of שקלים for one year. Everyone agrees both sets are holy. The argument is whether the extra set can cover next year's obligation. The ת״ק says no, so the city must give again next year. רבי יהודה says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: the thieves
these and those (both sets)
they count for them (they fulfill the obligation)
the next year

phrases.english: If they were found, or the thieves returned them —
both these and those are שקלים (holy),
and they do not count for them toward next year.
phrases.notes: The city must give new שקלים next year.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
They do count for them toward next year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה quoted in step 12, now covering the case where the coins are recovered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sets are holy. The ת״ק says the extra set does not count for next year. רבי יהודה says it does.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה say the coins count for next year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה lets this year's coins cover next year. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, each year's שקלים belong to that year. So it is surprising that money given for this year could cover next year. The גמרא wants the principle behind this.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יהודה's ruling in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle that lets this year's שקלים count for next year, according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבא explains: this year's offerings can be brought next year
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יהודה holds that a year's communal obligations may be offered in the following year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יהודה holds that the obligations (offerings) of this year can be brought next year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. He explains that for רבי יהודה, a year's offerings are not locked to that year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an offering meant for this year can be brought next year, then money collected for this year can also serve next year. That is why the extra שקלים count. This gives רבי יהודה a broad principle, and the next step will test it.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds (his opinion is)
obligations (required offerings)
are offered / brought

phrases.english: רבא said:
רבי יהודה holds
that the obligations of this year
are offered in the next year.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה holds that this year's obligations may be brought next year, so this year's money can cover next year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the claim that אביי attacks next, using רבי יהודה's ruling about lost and replaced יום הכפורים offerings.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from lost יום הכפורים offerings
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says lost-and-replaced communal sin-offerings must be left to die. If this year's offerings could be brought next year, why not save them for next year?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: If the bull and goat of יום הכפורים were lost, and he set aside others in their place, and the same if the goats for communal idol worship were lost and others were set aside, and then the first ones were found, all of them must be left to die. That is רבי יהודה's view. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון say: they graze until they get a blemish, then they are sold, and the money goes to a voluntary offering, because a communal חטאת is never left to die. רבא said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation using a ברייתא that seems to show רבי יהודה does not hold that this year's offerings can be brought next year. This passage ends with the words that introduce רבא's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה says the found animals must die. They cannot just wait and be offered next יום הכפורים. If he held that this year's obligations can be brought next year, he should have said to save them. So רבא's explanation seems to contradict רבי יהודה's own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a source)
he set aside other animals in their place
they must die (be left to die)
they graze until they become blemished
a voluntary offering
a communal sin-offering

steps.confusionAlert: Both sets of animals here are communal sin-offerings. The dispute is not about whether they are holy. It is about what happens to the extra ones: left to die (רבי יהודה), or sold for a נדבה (רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: אביי raised an objection to him:
The bull and goat of יום הכפורים
that were lost, and he set aside others in their place,
and likewise the goats for communal idol worship
that were lost, and he set aside others in their place —
all of them must be left to die; these are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון say:
They graze until they become blemished,
and they are sold, and their money goes to a voluntary offering,
because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.
He (רבא) said to him:
phrases.notes: This introduces רבא's reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי יהודה holds this year's obligations may be brought next year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה rules that found communal sin-offerings must die. If they could be offered next year, they should be saved instead. So רבי יהודה seems not to hold רבא's principle.
